name: OpenAI
summary: OpenAI launched GPT-6 Astra in September as its top model for computer use, coding and cyber work, then GPT-6.1 Sol as a cheaper near-Astra tier. DevDay recast ChatGPT as an agent platform led by always-on Dots. Revenue comes from ChatGPT subscriptions, including a new $500 Pro tier, plus the API.
bets: Dots: persistent background agents using cloud computers across 4,000+ apps
ChatGPT as enterprise agent hub: Marketplace, Spaces, Slack/Teams, computer-use Agents API
Scaling pretraining at Stargate Texas; Astra was its first run above 100,000 GPUs
Accepting less monitorable recurrent reasoning as a trade-off, drawing safety criticism

name: Anthropic
summary: Anthropic's Claude 5.5 family (Opus, Sonnet, and October's low-cost Haiku 5.5) brings near top-tier performance at lower prices for agentic coding, knowledge work and computer use. Fable 5.1 is its strongest general release; Mythos 5.1, the same model with fewer safeguards, is limited to vetted US defenders and life scientists. Revenue comes from the API and subscriptions.
bets: Restricted Mythos access for defensive vulnerability hunting through Project Glasswing
Unified Claude app merging Cowork into chat, plus Marketplace and Plugins ecosystem
Vertical editions: Government, Financial Advisors, Small Business, K-12 Teachers
Science push: life sciences verification program and Claude-driven biology discoveries

name: Google DeepMind
summary: Google DeepMind unveiled Gemini 4 Argon on September 30 for software engineering, legal and finance work, and cyber defense, with 1M-token output. After vetted defenders went first, Argon opened October 13 to paid API developers, enterprises, and Pro and Ultra subscribers. Google also ships Flash models, science and robotics work, monetized through the API, subscriptions and products.
bets: Phased Argon rollout: cyber defenders first, then API, enterprise and subscriber access in October
Flash-first strategy; Gemini 3.5 Pro skipped to focus on Gemini 4
Robotics via Gemini Robotics 2 and ER 2, now open in the Gemini API
AI for science: AlphaGenome Atlas, WeatherNext 3, Genesis Mission funding

name: Meta
summary: Meta Superintelligence Labs began with the closed Muse Spark in April, then iterated it and added the Muse Code agent. In October it launched Muse Wonder, its most capable models, and released Muse Spark Open, an 816B open-weight model with restrictions on large API resellers. Meta's ad business funds the work; models reach users through its apps and an API.
bets: Personal superintelligence delivered via WhatsApp, Instagram, Facebook and smart glasses
Frontier closed models (Muse Wonder) alongside open-weight releases like Muse Spark Open
Small open models running always-on local agents on one consumer GPU
Long-horizon coding agents with persistent sub-agents (Muse Code)

name: xAI (SpaceXAI)
summary: SpaceX acquired xAI in February 2026 and the lab rebranded as SpaceXAI in July, hence OpenRouter's new label. It bought Cursor for $60B in August and now ships coding-focused Grok models, most recently Grok 4.7, through Grok Build, Cursor, the API and X. Business mixes consumer Grok and X with paid API access.
bets: Orbital solar-powered data centers; FCC filing for up to one million compute satellites
Using Cursor's data and distribution to compete in coding agents
Huge GPU fleet as training edge; Colossus expansion toward one million GPUs
Long-running tasks with self-checking, plus a rebuilt safeguard stack in Grok 4.7

name: Alibaba (Qwen)
summary: Alibaba runs a dual track: open-weight Qwen releases, such as August's 2.4T Qwen3.8 MoE and an Apache-licensed 27B, alongside proprietary Max and Plus models sold through Alibaba Cloud. At September's Apsara conference it said Qwen 4 is in training and laid out a full-stack roadmap across models, chips and cloud.
bets: Qwen 4.5 and Qwen 5 scaled to 5-10 trillion parameters
Recursive self-improvement research, shown with automated Qwen3.8-Max training cycles
Over 20 GW of data center capacity by 2032; new overseas cloud regions
In-house T-Head Zhenwu V900 chip, production planned for Q1 2027

name: DeepSeek
summary: DeepSeek released V4 in April as open weights, a 1.6T-parameter Pro and 284B Flash, making 1M-token context the default, then tuned both for agents over the summer. September's V4.1-Flash added native vision and cut API prices. It pairs open weights with a cheap API and free chat app, and says little about future plans.
bets: Agentic coding compatibility: Responses API for Codex, works with Claude Code
New architecture family starting with V4.1-Flash, built to scale larger
Aggressive pricing, including off-peak discounts at half the peak rate

name: Moonshot AI
summary: Moonshot's July release, Kimi K3 (2.8T parameters), is billed as the first open 3T-class model and competes with US frontier systems on agentic and coding work. Weights are downloadable, but large commercial API providers must sign a separate agreement; Moonshot also sells API access and runs the Kimi app.
bets: Agent Swarm: hundreds of parallel sub-agents for research and long tasks
Kimi Code tooling to win developer and enterprise coding contracts
Preparing a Hong Kong IPO after large 2026 funding rounds

name: Z.ai
summary: Z.ai, listed in Hong Kong since January, has kept a fast GLM-5.x cadence: GLM-5.1 for long autonomous tasks, GLM-5.2 with 1M-token context, and August's coding-focused GLM-5.3 plus a vision-capable Flash. It sells API access and pitches its models as open-source leaders on coding benchmarks.
bets: Long-horizon agents; GLM-5.1 works autonomously for up to eight hours
ZCode IDE that also supports OpenAI and Anthropic models
Running on domestic chips such as Cambricon and Moore Threads
Raising API prices despite earlier compute shortages

name: MiniMax
summary: MiniMax, public in Hong Kong since January, launched the open-weight M3 in June: a 1M-context, natively multimodal model aimed at agentic coding and computer use, built on its own sparse attention. A video model, H3, followed in July. It monetizes through API token plans and consumer apps such as Talkie.
bets: MiniMax Sparse Attention to make 1M-token context far cheaper
Agentic coding plus autonomous desktop computer operation in one model
Multimodal video generation alongside its language models

name: Mistral AI
summary: Mistral is recasting itself as a sovereign European AI stack: open-weight models plus its own compute in France and Sweden. In September it raised EUR 3B led by Samsung. On October 6 it opened a preview API for Mistral Large 4, a 1T-parameter multimodal MoE trained in its own datacenters, with weights promised by month's end.
bets: Releasing Large 4 weights, a 1T-parameter open model trained on its own European compute
About EUR 4B in data centers; positioning as a cloud company
Industrial deals: Samsung semiconductor AI, new Munich hub
Co-developing the Nemotron Coalition base model with NVIDIA

name: NVIDIA
summary: NVIDIA's business is AI hardware, and its Vera Rubin platform entered mass production in mid-2026. It also builds open Nemotron models to strengthen the ecosystem: the 550B Nemotron 3 Ultra shipped in June, emphasizing fast token generation, and a trillion-plus-parameter Nemotron 4 is in training.
bets: Nemotron 4 with at least 1T parameters, possibly ready by late fall
Nemotron Coalition of labs co-building an open base model on DGX Cloud
Vera Rubin systems aimed at agentic AI workloads
AI PC push: RTX Spark laptop chip and DGX Station

name: Thinking Machines
summary: Mira Murati's lab released its first broadly available model, Inkling, in July: a 975B open-weights multimodal MoE under Apache 2.0 with adjustable thinking effort, followed by a distilled Inkling Small. Its business centers on customization through the Tinker fine-tuning API, with hosted inference via partner clouds.
bets: Real-time interaction model handling audio, video and text in 200ms chunks
Tinker fine-tuning as core product across many open model families
1 GW of NVIDIA Vera Rubin compute via strategic partnership

name: ByteDance Seed
summary: ByteDance Seed builds the models behind the Doubao chatbot and Volcano Engine cloud. Its Seed 2.1 family is pitched as an agent for real-world productivity, while the team keeps pushing generative media and full-duplex audio-video interaction. Models are largely proprietary, monetized through apps, new Doubao subscriptions and cloud APIs.
bets: Seed 2.1 as a general productivity agent rather than a chatbot
Longer, controllable video: 30-second Seedance 2.5 clips with many references
Real-time full-duplex audio-visual interaction model
Doubao subscription tiers on a 330M-user base
